summary: High-fidelity two-qubit gates are demonstrated in a 7-qubit NV-center register in diamond, achieving average fidelity of 99.18(2)% and best-case 99.61(5)% using dynamically decoupled radiofrequency (DDRF) gates on nuclear spins coupled to the NV electron spin. The work characterizes crosstalk mechanisms, develops an efficient gate optimization procedure, and validates the gates with variational quantum eigensolver simulations of H$_2$ and LiH molecules, demonstrating performance at the threshold for distributed quantum computation.
motivation: Quantum networks based on optically active solid-state spins require multiple high-fidelity qubits per node to approach fault-tolerance thresholds (~99.4% for distributed surface codes with 3–6 qubits), but multi-qubit crosstalk and parameter optimization in highly connected systems have hindered progress.
method: The authors systematically analyze three crosstalk mechanisms (conditional RF driving of idling spins, unconditional RF driving, and dynamical-decoupling interactions through perpendicular hyperfine coupling), develop a four-step experimental optimization procedure sweeping interpulse delay $\tau$ while checking for DD resonances and measuring 7-qubit state fidelity, and characterize gates using two-qubit gate set tomography on six separate electron–nuclear-spin pairs.
result: Average two-qubit DDRF gate fidelity of 99.18(2)% over six nuclear spins (best: $e$–$^{14}$N gate at 99.61(5)%), with stochastic phase errors on the electron dominating infidelity; VQE demonstrates ground-state energy estimation for H$_2$ (chemical accuracy at one spacing) and LiH using 4–5 qubits with Clifford fitting error mitigation.
